abstract: The mammalian embryo implantation is generally regulated by ovarian estrogen and progesterone in laboratory animals so far studied. In some animals, like golden hamsters, the process of implantation is reported to be independent of ovarian estrogen. Other studies, however, suggest that estrogen-related events do exist for implantation. We also observed the complete absence of implantation in letrozole-treated uterine horns (an inhibitor of the key enzyme for estrogen biosynthesis). However, the vehicle-treated horn bear has a normal implantation site in D6 of pregnancy. Hence, there must be an involvement of estrogen that may come from a source other than the ovary. It may be either non-ovarian or locally synthesized (non-systemic, uterine). But the involvement of non-systemic estrogen is not well documented. So, in the present study, the de novo synthesis of estrogen in the uterus and its role in early pregnancy is described. For this, letrozole-treated and control uterine horns were further studied using the tools of proteomics and genomics to know the exact cause of failure of implantation. Using IHC, it was observed that there is a presence of cytochrome P450 aromatase, a rate-limiting enzyme in the estrogen biosynthesis pathway, in the uterine horn of pregnant hamsters at the time of implantation. The expression profile of this enzyme and their mRNA was further checked by western blot and real-time PCR, respectively. It also corroborated earlier IHC observations. We found that their expression is markedly induced at the implantation site and in stromal cells around the day of implantation and decidualization, respectively. This aromatase is responsible for de novo synthesis of estrogen in association with other steroidogenic enzymes, which was also observed to be present in the uterus during early pregnancy. This locally synthesized estrogen is sufficient to elicit other implantation-specific physiological factors required for successful embryo implantation and decidualization in the absence of ovarian estrogen. Since embryo implantation in human beings is also ovarian estrogen independent and much more similar to hamster, so, this study may help in managing issue concerning to infertility in women due to early loss of pregnancy.
